children: Ola Electric sets the rights issue price at Rs 27 per share, a discount of around 26 per cent to the reference price cited in its announcement

Ola Electric Mobility shares fell nearly 3 per cent in early trade on Tuesday as the stock turned ex-rights ahead of the company’s planned Rs 999.74-crore fundraising exercise. The decline came after the shares had gained over the previous two trading sessions.

The stock fell 2.9 per cent to Rs 34.64 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), compared with Monday’s close of Rs 35.68. Ola Electric shares had risen from Rs 34.63 on 8 October to Rs 35.13 on 9 October before extending gains in the previous session.

The ex-date is the first day on which shares trade without the entitlement to participate in the rights issue. The price adjustment around this date should therefore be distinguished from a decline driven purely by market sentiment.

Ola Electric has set the rights issue price at Rs 27 per share, a discount of around 26 per cent to the reference price cited in its announcement. The issue will open on 22 October and close on 30 October.
Eligible shareholders will be entitled to apply for two equity shares for every 25 shares held on the record date. The offering is intended to raise Rs 999.74 crore.

The company plans to use around Rs 350 crore towards repayment or prepayment of debt and Rs 400 crore to fund organic growth initiatives. The remaining proceeds will be allocated to general corporate purposes.

The fundraising comes as the electric two-wheeler maker seeks to strengthen its balance sheet while continuing to invest in its business. Investor participation in the issue will be a key indicator of shareholder support for the company’s funding plans.

Despite the gains in the two preceding sessions, Ola Electric shares have remained under pressure over a longer period. The stock has fallen around 10.4 per cent over the past month and 7.97 per cent so far in 2026. It is down 31.31 per cent over the past year.
The shares have traded between Rs 22.25 and Rs 57.95 over the past 52 weeks, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 17,305.4 crore.

Investors will now track the rights issue as well as the company’s progress in managing debt and financing growth. The discounted issue price provides eligible shareholders an opportunity to subscribe at a lower price, but the broader investment case will continue to depend on Ola Electric’s financial performance and execution.
